Contrary to popular belief, the snapdragon 615 is not just an 8-core CPU running the full software stack. There are multiple CPU units in the SOC, things like a dedicated hardware for video and image processing, DSP and modem subsystems etc.

There is currently no open-source software that can power any of these custom modules. The drivers for these modules are baked deep into the kernel and often even spill out into the userspace. These are usually android-only and are not found in pure Linux distros.

My guess is that you will at best, brick huge chunks of snapdragon 615. I wouldn't recommend it if that's the only phone you have.

If you want to play around though, try something like https://developer.qualcomm.com/hardware/dragonboard-410c

There is a Linux version that's supported I think and you can play around.

Source: I write software for the snapdragons.
